description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the SCOPE-WRAPPING metamorphic run (every battery program wrapped in a string eval, the wrapping VALIDATED by perl): 3 of the 7 silent differences are this.  Minimal, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/eval-local1.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main:

    eval q{ our $x = 1; sub showA { print "A: $x\n" } sub tA { local $x = 2; showA() } tA(); showA(); };
        perl: A: 2 / A: 1        PCL: A: 1 / A: 1
    our $y = 1; eval q{ sub showB { print "B: $y\n" } sub tB { local $y = 2; showB() } }; tB();
        perl: B: 2               PCL: B: 1
    eval q{ our @a = (1,2,3); sub showC {...} sub tC { local @a = (9); showC() } tC(); };      perl 9, PCL 1 2 3
    eval q{ $main::z = 1; sub showD { print $main::z } sub tD { local $main::z = 2; showD() } tD(); };   BOTH right

So the FULLY QUALIFIED spelling is right and the unqualified one is not: in eval mode the `local` target and the sibling sub's read resolve to DIFFERENT cells (the capture-alist / package-cell split the memory notes describe: block-scoped vs FILE-level lexicals reach an eval by different mechanisms; an `our` alias may be a third).  The same program OUTSIDE an eval is right (control G in the probe).
MEASURE FIRST: the emission of `local $x` and of `$x` in showA inside the eval (which symbol each names).  The detector/rewriter/promoter must share ONE resolver (standing rule).  A name-resolution change => the full sweep IS the gate + gate-SET scan; string eval is in 55 of 111 perl-tests files.
Edges seen in the same run, NOT this bug (note, do not chase here): `wantarray()` at the top level of a string eval is "" where perl has undef; `(caller)[2]` inside an eval; FindBin inside an eval.
subject: SILENT WRONG: inside a STRING EVAL, `local $x` / `local @a` on an UNQUALIFIED package variable does not reach what another sub reads -- config/plugin code evaluated from a string loses every `local`
